title: Review: Momentum and its conservation; Moments and static equilibrium; Systems and centre of mass; Work done; Kinetic and potential energy; conservation; Work–energy theorem and dissipative forces; Power and efficiency; Charge and current
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: E03-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; EL01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; E03-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; EL01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D07-1#N.2, D08-1#N.5a, D09-1#N.7, D09-2#N.3, E01-1#N.9b, E02-1#N.12, E03-1#N.15, E04-1#N.6b, EL01-1#N.3, D07-1#N.5, D08-1#N.2, D09-1#N.2. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Power
items.clue: Rate of doing work, or rate of energy transfer.

items.label: Current
items.clue: Rate of flow of charge through a cross-section.

items.label: Watt
items.clue: Unit equal to one joule transferred each second.

items.label: Coulomb
items.clue: Unit: the amount passing a place in a wire when 1 A flows for 1 s.

questions.stem: A cylindrical rod is made of a 0.50 m aluminium section joined end to end to a 0.50 m steel section of the same diameter. Each section is uniform, and the steel section has the greater mass. How does the location of the rod's centre of mass compare with the rod's midpoint?

options.text: It is at the midpoint, since the rod's shape is symmetric about that point.
It is on the aluminium side of the midpoint, nearer the lighter section.
It is at the centre of the steel section, the more massive part.
It lies between the midpoint and the centre of the steel section.

questions.stem: A uniform beam of length 5.0 m and weight 400 N rests horizontally on two supports, one at each end, P and Q. A person of weight 600 N stands on the beam 1.0 m from Q. What is the upward force from support P?
questions.explanation: Taking moments about Q: F_P × 5.0 = 400 × 2.5 + 600 × 1.0 = 1600 N m, so F_P = 320 N.

questions.stem: Two blocks, of masses 1.0 kg and 4.0 kg, are held at rest on a horizontal surface with negligible friction, with a compressed spring between them. When they are released, the 1.0 kg block moves off at 2.0 m s⁻¹. Which statement about the 4.0 kg block is correct?

options.text: It moves off at 2.0 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It moves off at 0.50 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It moves off at 8.0 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It stays at rest, as the total momentum must stay zero.

questions.explanation: Total momentum starts at zero and stays zero: 4.0 × v = 1.0 × 2.0, so v = 0.50 m s⁻¹, opposite to the 1.0 kg block.

questions.stem: A 0.50 kg trolley moving at 5.0 m s⁻¹ collides with a 3.0 kg trolley at rest on a level track with negligible friction. After the collision, the 0.50 kg trolley moves backwards at 1.0 m s⁻¹ and the 3.0 kg trolley moves forwards at 1.0 m s⁻¹. How much of the system's kinetic energy is transformed into other forms of energy?

A student carries a bag of weight 15 N up a flight of stairs at constant velocity. The bag moves 4.0 m horizontally and rises 3.0 m, so it travels 5.0 m along the stairs. How much work does the student's upward force do on the bag?

options.text: 60 J, the upward force multiplied by the horizontal distance.
45 J, the upward force multiplied by the height gained.
75 J, the upward force multiplied by the distance along the stairs.
Zero, as the bag moves at constant velocity, so no work is done on it.

questions.explanation: The force is vertical and the displacement is 5.0 m at an angle θ to it, with cos θ = 3.0/5.0. Work = 15 × 5.0 × 0.60 = 45 J: the force times the 3.0 m rise.

questions.stem: Three identical stones are thrown from the top of a sea cliff with the same speed: one straight up, one horizontally and one straight down. Air resistance is negligible. Which stone hits the sea with the greatest speed?

options.text: The one thrown straight down, as its velocity starts in the direction of gravity.
The one thrown upwards, as it falls back from a greater height than the others.
The one thrown horizontally, as it keeps its horizontal speed while gaining vertical speed.
All land at equal speeds: same starting kinetic energy, same drop in height.

questions.explanation: Initial kinetic energy + potential energy lost = final kinetic energy, and both terms are equal for all three stones. The speeds are equal; only the directions and times of flight differ.

questions.stem: Motor A raises a 200 N load through 3.0 m in 6.0 s. Motor B raises a 100 N load through 6.0 m in 4.0 s. Both lift at constant speed. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A develops more power, as it lifts the heavier load.
B does more work, as it lifts its load twice as high.
Both do equal work, and B develops more power.
Both develop equal power, as they do equal work.

questions.explanation: Each does 600 J (200 × 3.0 and 100 × 6.0). B does it in less time: 600 ÷ 4.0 = 150 W against 600 ÷ 6.0 = 100 W.

questions.stem: A skier of mass 60 kg starts from rest at the top of a slope and descends through a vertical height of 20 m. At the bottom her speed is 16 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the total work done on the skier by friction and air resistance during the descent?

In an electron beam in a vacuum tube, 1.5 × 10¹⁵ electrons pass through a cross-section of the beam in 8.0 s at a steady rate. What is the magnitude of the current in the beam? Use e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
A rectangular wooden sign hangs from a single hook through a hole at the middle of its top edge. A heavy metal letter is fixed near the sign's left end. How does the sign hang at rest?

options.text: Level, because the hook is at the middle of the top edge.
Tilted, left end lower, with its centre of gravity directly below the hook.
Tilted, left end lower, until the metal letter is directly below the hook.
Tilted, right end lower, to balance the heavy letter.

questions.explanation: At rest the weight has no moment about the hook, so its line of action passes through the hook. The sign turns until its centre of gravity, shifted left by the letter, is vertically below the hook.

questions.stem: A mechanic pulls with a 20 N force on the end of a tool handle, 0.25 m from the centre of a nut. The force is in the plane of the handle's turn, but at 30° to the handle instead of at 90°. What is the turning effect of the force about the centre of the nut?

options.text: 5.0 N m
4.3 N m
80 N m
2.5 N m

questions.explanation: Perpendicular distance = 0.25 × sin 30° = 0.125 m, so the turning effect = 20 × 0.125 = 2.5 N m.

questions.stem: A cricket ball of mass m moving horizontally with speed v is struck by a bat. It leaves the bat moving horizontally with speed 3v/2 in the opposite direction. Taking the ball's initial direction of motion as positive, what is the change in the ball's momentum?
